title: Real-Time Dashboard authoring and Multi Stat/KPI design
summary: Generate a blank documented RealTimeDashboard.json definition offline, then author version-matched visuals and validate data, layout, permissions and rendering separately. Multi Stat consumes label/value rows; KPI is a single metric, not Power BI report authoring.
contract: kql-dashboard scaffold --title <TITLE> is offline and creates no Fabric item. It returns definition.parts with canonical RealTimeDashboard.json/InlineBase64, a schema-52 blank page and time-range parameter, no data sources/queries/tiles, and autoRefresh disabled. scaffoldOnly:true/renderingVerified:false are explicit. It is not a new visualization engine or latest-schema converter.

Save the data payload rather than the fabio envelope: fabio kql-dashboard scaffold --title 'Overview' --query definition -o plain > definition.json. Existing update-definition accepts this parts object; preview replacement with --dry-run before approval. Never apply a blank scaffold over an existing populated dashboard without an approved backup/replacement plan.

The public REST definition article shows schema_version as string '52'; the versioned schema describes pages, queries, queryRef and multiStat__ visual options. Newer exports can have different schemas and version types. Keep an existing export's version and unknown fields. Do not mix v20 inline query fields with v52 queryRef or infer new KPI-mode fields from UI labels.

This initial generator deliberately does not fabricate advanced tiles. For Multi Stat, run a query returning label/value rows, select Label column and Value column in the target editor, then choose grid/orientation/text size and export the verified definition. A synthetic design query is: datatable(Metric:string, Value:long) ['Active',42,'Mitigated',18,'Resolved',73]. These are examples, not measured health values.

KPI shows one query-derived numeric value with explicit target/healthy-warning-critical thresholds; Multi Stat shows multiple metrics in a grid. Define units, direction of improvement, null/stale/no-data behavior and time windows before choosing colors. Avoid mixing incomparable units or signaling health from arbitrary example values.

Design an Overview page with concise headline metrics, a trend row and drill-down details; use readable labels, consistent spacing, restrained colors and non-color status cues. Filter early with reviewed time parameters and bound expensive query ranges. Refresh remains opt-in because it consumes capacity.

Validate query results and data-source scope/permissions separately from successful definition upload. Re-open in the target dashboard UI and check narrow/wide layouts, labels, units, thresholds and accessibility. REST round-trip is not proof of visual rendering or source readiness; no screenshots or UI rendering are claimed by scaffold.
Real-Time Dashboard maps to kql-dashboard (KQLDashboard), not Power BI dashboard/report or semantic-model authoring.
